what: independent re-verification evidence that the notice face has been mounted in a real, non-headless window -- not only in the headless renderer tools/shoot.mjs and tools/browser-mount-smoke.mjs already drive
why: req/02 W15 clause 3, applied to this face as part of an independent re-verification lane: a face must carry proof of having mounted in a real window a person could look at. This record and the two capture files beside it were produced fresh by the re-verification lane (2026-08-24), authored from zero -- tools/browser-mount-smoke.mjs and tools/real-window-smoke.mjs in this same faces/notice/tools/ directory were written without opening faces/ledger's versions, following only the shape the dispatching brief described (fixture served over http + shell/tools/real_window.ps1, the shell's own real-window instrument, reused rather than duplicated).
how: tools/real-window-smoke.mjs starts a static file server rooted at the repo (answering /s-common/tokens.css from the one stylesheet of record, the same route name shell/tools/serve.mjs answers), then shells out to shell/tools/real_window.ps1 with the fixture's URL. That script opens Chrome in app mode at 1440x900, waits, reads the window's own title back through the Win32 window list, and screenshots the on-screen window rectangle. This face's mount fixture (fixtures/mount-entry.mjs + fixtures/mount.html) imports index.mjs directly and calls mount(host, {}, notices) with nine notice entries spelled out inline in the fixture -- one of every outcome word this face draws plus one non-record string -- and writes the element/data-entry counts into document.title so the numbers below are the numbers the page itself computed, not typed by hand. The script itself only returns numbers and writes the two PNGs; it does not overwrite this file -- the JSON below is this record, written once by the agent that looked at the pictures.
